mainTopic: The קטורת's preparation and ingredients, and the laws of smearing שמן המשחה
overview: This amud opens with ברייתות about the קטורת. Leftover incense sometimes let the Temple prepare only half a year's batch, so רבן שמעון בן גמליאל rules that a private person who copies half the recipe is liable. The חכמים say it was prepared daily in proportion, which supports רבא. The קטורת was re-ground twice a year and ground with the chant 'crush well, well crush,' which supports רבי יוחנן's idea that speech is good for spices. The יום הכפורים portion was ground extra fine. רבי יוחנן says the incense has eleven ingredients, and the גמרא defends רב הונא's count from the פסוק against a כלל ופרט וכלל reading. It also explains why only items whose smoke rises qualify, and ריש לקיש learns this from the word קטורת itself. A side teaching uses bad-smelling חלבנה to show that a communal fast must include sinners. The גמרא then turns to smearing שמן המשחה. It explains why animals, vessels, corpses and gentiles are exempt. רב יוסף then explains the disputes between רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה about the amount of oil and about already-anointed kings and כהנים. The amud ends as רב איקא begins to show that both תנאים follow their own reasoning elsewhere, with the source continuing on the next amud.

steps.title: Leftover incense let them prepare half a batch
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that leftover קטורת built up over time, so every sixty or seventy years the Temple prepared only half the yearly amount.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: Because of the leftover incense, once every sixty or seventy years they would prepare it in halves.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא with a historical fact about the Temple: sometimes they made only half the usual yearly batch of קטורת. This fact is the setup for the legal ruling that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Every year a little extra קטורת was made, and the unused part was saved. After many decades the saved amount added up to half a year's supply. So that year they only needed to prepare the other half.

keyTerms.meaning: The leftover incense that was not used up
Blending or compounding the spices of the incense
In halves, meaning half of the usual amount

phrases.english: The Sages taught: The leftover of the incense,
once every sixty or seventy years,
they would blend it in halves.
phrases.notes: The saved-up leftovers covered half the year, so they only had to make the other half fresh.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about preparing the קטורת in partial amounts.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Once every sixty or seventy years, the Temple prepared the קטורת in a half-batch because of the leftovers.

steps.title: A private person who blends half the recipe is liable
steps.stepSummary: Because the Temple sometimes made half-batches, a private person who makes a half-batch has made a real 'Temple recipe' and is liable. רבן שמעון בן גמליאל says this in the name of the סגן, but adds that he never heard a ruling about a third or a quarter.
steps.simpleTranslation: Therefore, an individual who blended the incense in halves is liable. These are the words of רבן שמעון בן גמליאל, who said it in the name of the deputy High Priest. But about a third or a quarter, I did not hear.
steps.whatsHappening: From the historical fact, רבן שמעון בן גמליאל draws a legal rule: copying the קטורת in a half-amount for private use is forbidden and makes one liable. He then limits what he knows: smaller fractions were never part of his tradition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The תורה forbids making the קטורת for yourself 'according to its recipe.' Since the Temple itself sometimes made exactly half a batch, a half-batch counts as a real Temple recipe. Rashi explains that the Temple never needed to make just a third or a quarter, so there was no tradition about it, and one who makes that amount is פטור.

keyTerms.meaning: A private individual, not acting for the Temple
Liable, meaning he has broken the prohibition
The deputy of the כהן גדול
A third and a quarter of the full amount

steps.confusionAlert: 'I did not hear' does not mean he rules a third or a quarter is allowed. It only means he has no tradition about those amounts.

phrases.english: Therefore, an individual who blended it in halves is liable,
these are the words of Rabban Shimon ben Gamliel,
who said it in the name of the deputy High Priest.
But about a third or a quarter, I did not hear.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a legal ruling ('therefore') from the historical fact in step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A private person who prepares a half-batch of the קטורת is liable; no tradition exists for a third or a quarter.

steps.title: The Sages: incense was prepared each day in proportion
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say that every day the קטורת was prepared in its proper proportions and brought in to be burned.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the Sages say: Every day he would prepare it according to its recipe, and he would bring it in.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים give a different picture: the Temple did not only make whole or half batches. Each day's small amount was prepared in the correct ratio of ingredients.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If each day's portion was made in the right proportions, then even a small amount counts as a real Temple recipe. This sets up the גמרא's next point, that the חכמים support רבא.

keyTerms.meaning: Brings in, into the היכל to burn on the מזבח הזהב

phrases.aramaic: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בְּכׇל יוֹם מְתַקֵּן בְּמַתְכּוּנְתָּהּ,
phrases.english: And the Sages say: Every day he would prepare it according to its recipe,
and he would bring it in.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַחֲכָמִים אוֹמְרִים: בְּכׇל יוֹם מְתַקֵּן בְּמַתְכּוּנְתָּהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the חכמים's differing view on how the קטורת was prepared.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת was prepared each day in proper proportions, so even a small portion counts as the Temple's recipe.

steps.title: The Sages' view supports רבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says the חכמים's view supports רבא, who ruled about preparing in halves.
steps.simpleTranslation: This supports רבא, as רבא said: The anointing oil that one blended in halves, he is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out that the חכמים in the ברייתא agree with a later ruling of רבא. It then quotes רבא's ruling.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבא holds that making a partial amount can still make one liable. The חכמים said each daily portion was a proper recipe, which backs this up. The full point of רבא's ruling is about the קטורת, as his פסוק in the next step shows.
steps.confusionAlert: The פסוק רבא quotes next is about the קטורת, not the oil. So his main ruling is that the קטורת made in portions makes one liable.

phrases.english: This supports Rava, as Rava said:
The anointing oil that one blended in halves — he is liable,
phrases.notes: The real point is that making the oil in portions is exempt, but making the קטורת in portions is liable. That fits the פסוק about incense quoted next.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Uses the חכמים's view from step 3 as support for רבא.
steps.raayaObject: רבא's ruling that preparing in portions can make one liable
steps.raayaSupportSource: The חכמים's statement that the קטורת was prepared each day in its proportions

steps.title: רבא's source: any amount the Temple makes
steps.stepSummary: רבא learns from 'and the incense that you shall make' that any amount the Temple actually makes is forbidden to copy, and the Temple did make half-portions: half in the morning and half in the afternoon.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is written: 'And the incense that you shall make' — anything that you make. And it is possible to make a portion in the morning and a portion in the afternoon.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא gives his source from the פסוק. Whatever amount of קטורת is made for the Temple is forbidden to copy, and since a half-portion is used each morning and evening, that amount counts too.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'that you shall make' are read as 'whatever you make' for the Temple. The daily קטורת was split, half burned in the morning and half in the afternoon. So a portion that small is a real Temple amount, and copying it makes one liable.

keyTerms.meaning: Anything that you make, any amount made for the Temple
A portion, here half of a מנה

steps.whatToRemember: According to רבא, copying even a portion of the קטורת makes one liable, because the Temple itself made and used portions that small: half in the morning, half in the afternoon.

phrases.english: as it is written: 'And the incense that you shall make' —
phrases.notes: שמות 30:37

phrases.english: anything that you make,
and it is possible to make it as a portion in the morning
and a portion in the afternoon.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the פסוק behind רבא's ruling from step 4.
steps.raayaObject: Liability for preparing the קטורת in portions
steps.raayaSupportSource: שמות 30:37, 'and the incense that you shall make,' together with the morning and afternoon half-portions

steps.title: Re-grinding the incense and storing it by season
steps.stepSummary: A new ברייתא teaches that the קטורת was put back in the mortar twice a year, spread out in summer to avoid mold and piled up in the rainy season to keep its scent.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Sages taught: They would return it to the mortar twice a year. In the summer it was kept spread out so it would not get moldy; in the rainy season it was kept piled up so its scent would not fade.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new ברייתא about caring for the stored קטורת. It explains how often it was re-ground and how it was kept in each season.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Stored spices can spoil. In hot weather a pile can get moldy, so it was spread out. In the rainy season a spread-out layer can lose its smell, so it was piled together.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתָהּ לְמַכְתֶּשֶׁת
phrases.english: The Sages taught: They would return it to the mortar
twice a year,
in the summer, spread out — so that it will not grow moldy,

phrases.aramaic: בִּימוֹת הַגְּשָׁמִים צְבוּרָה – כְּדֵי שֶׁלֹּא תָּפוּג רֵיחָהּ.
phrases.english: in the rainy season, piled up — so that its scent will not fade.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הָיוּ מַחֲזִירִין אוֹתָהּ לְמַכְתֶּשֶׁת
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new ברייתא about storing and re-grinding the קטורת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת was re-ground twice a year, spread out in summer and piled up in the rainy season.

steps.title: The grinder's chant: crush well, well crush
steps.stepSummary: While grinding the קטורת, the person would say 'crush well, well crush,' according to אבא יוסי בן יוחנן.
steps.simpleTranslation: And when he grinds, he says: 'Crush well, well crush.' These are the words of Abba Yosei ben Yochanan.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא adds a detail about the grinding itself: the worker said a short chant while crushing the spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'crush well, well crush' repeat the same idea back and forth, encouraging a fine, careful grind. This finishes the description of how the קטורת was looked after.
steps.whatToRemember: The stored קטורת was carefully maintained: re-ground twice a year, stored by season, and ground with the chant 'crush well, well crush.'

phrases.english: And when he grinds, he says:
'Crush well, well crush,'
these are the words of Abba Yosei ben Yochanan.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּכְשֶׁהוּא שׁוֹחֵק, אוֹמֵר: הָדֵק הֵיטֵב, הֵיטֵב הָדֵק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a detail about how the grinding was done.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: While grinding the קטורת, one says 'crush well, well crush.'

steps.title: The three extra portions ground extra fine for יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: the three extra מנים used for the כהן גדול's handfuls on יום הכפורים were put back in the mortar on the day before and ground very fine.
steps.simpleTranslation: The three extra מנים, from which the כהן גדול takes his handfuls on יום הכפורים, were put into the mortar on the eve of יום הכפורים and ground very well, so they would be extra fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא keeps describing how the קטורת was handled, now focusing on the special portion for יום הכפורים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Besides the daily amounts, there were three extra מנים set aside for the כהן גדול to bring into the קודש הקדשים. This portion got a second grinding right before יום הכפורים so it would be finer than the regular קטורת.

keyTerms.meaning: Mortar, the bowl used for crushing

phrases.english: And the three extra maneh
from which the High Priest brings in
his full handfuls on Yom Kippur,
one places it into the mortar
on the eve of Yom Kippur,
and grinds them very, very well,
so that it will be the finest of the fine,

steps.triggerLanguage: וְשָׁלֹשׁ מָנִין יְתֵירִין שֶׁמֵּהֶן כֹּהֵן גָּדוֹל מַכְנִיס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ברייתא from steps 6-7 about returning the קטורת to the mortar.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The יום הכפורים portion is ground again on ערב יום הכפורים to be extra fine.

steps.title: The פסוק that requires extra-fine קטורת on יום הכפורים
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא shows that the word 'דקה' in the יום הכפורים section teaches an extra-fine grinding, since regular fine grinding was already commanded.
steps.simpleTranslation: As it is taught: Why does the פסוק say 'finely ground'? Didn't it already say 'and you shall grind some of it finely'? Why say 'finely ground' again? To teach that it must be the finest of the fine.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא as the source for the extra grinding described in the previous step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק in שמות already commands that all קטורת be ground fine. So when the יום הכפורים section says 'דקה' again, it must be adding something: an even finer grinding for that day.

keyTerms.meaning: Why does the פסוק need to say this?
Finest of the fine, extra fine

phrases.english: as it is taught in a baraita:
"Finely ground": why does the verse say this?
phrases.notes: ויקרא 16:12, about the קטורת on יום הכפורים.

phrases.english: Wasn't it already said:
"And you shall grind some of it finely"?
phrases.notes: שמות 30:36

phrases.english: So why does the verse say "finely ground"?
So that it will be the finest of the fine.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the scriptural source for the extra grinding in step 8.
steps.raayaObject: The rule that the יום הכפורים קטורת must be extra fine
steps.raayaSupportSource: The seemingly extra word 'דקה' in ויקרא 16:12, after 'הדק' in שמות 30:36
steps.whatToRemember: The regular קטורת is ground fine. The יום הכפורים portion is ground again to be the finest of the fine, learned from the extra word 'דקה'.

steps.title: Saying 'crush well' supports רבי יוחנן on speech and spices
steps.stepSummary: The custom of saying 'crush well, well crush' while grinding supports רבי יוחנן, who said speech is bad for wine but good for spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Master said: when he grinds, he says 'crush well, well crush.' This supports רבי יוחנן, who said: just as speech is bad for wine, speech is good for spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא goes back to a line from the ברייתא (step 7) and shows that it supports a statement of רבי יוחנן.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Talking while preparing wine harms it, but רבי יוחנן says talking while preparing spices helps them. The fact that the grinder of the קטורת deliberately spoke while working backs up רבי יוחנן's idea.

phrases.english: The Master said:
phrases.notes: He is quoting the ברייתא from step 7.

phrases.english: When he grinds, he says
"Crush well, well crush":
this supports Rabbi Yoḥanan,
as Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Just as speech is bad for wine,
so speech is good for spices.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the line in step 7 and links it to רבי יוחנן.
steps.raayaObject: רבי יוחנן's statement that speech is good for spices
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא's description of saying 'crush well, well crush' while grinding the קטורת

steps.title: Eleven ingredients were told to משה at סיני
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן teaches that the קטורת's eleven ingredients were told to משה at סיני.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: eleven ingredients were told to משה at סיני.
steps.whatsHappening: A new topic begins: how many ingredients are in the קטורת and where we know it from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only some ingredients are named outright in the פסוק. רבי יוחנן says the full number, eleven, was given to משה at סיני.

keyTerms.meaning: Were told to משה at סיני

phrases.english: Rabbi Yoḥanan said:
Eleven ingredients
were told to Moses at Sinai.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: אַחַד עָשָׂר סַמְמָנִין
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens a new topic: the number of ingredients in the קטורת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The קטורת has eleven ingredients, given to משה at סיני.

steps.title: רב הונא counts eleven ingredients from the פסוק
steps.stepSummary: רב הונא finds the number eleven in the פסוק: 'spices' (two) plus three named spices makes five, the second 'spices' doubles it to ten, and frankincense makes eleven.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הונא said: What is the פסוק? 'Take for you spices': two. 'Stacte, onycha, and galbanum': now five. The other 'spices': another five, now ten. 'Pure frankincense': one. That makes eleven.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הונא shows how the number eleven from step 11 can be read into the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plural 'spices' means at least two. Adding the three named spices gives five. The second 'spices' is read as 'the same amount again', making ten, and frankincense brings it to eleven.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the פסוק for this?
Galbanum, a resin with a sharp smell

steps.confusionAlert: The second 'סמים' does not mean one more spice. רב הונא reads it as doubling everything counted so far (five more), which is how we get from five to ten.

phrases.english: Rav Huna said: What is the verse?
"Take for you spices": two,
phrases.notes: שמות 30:34. 'Spices' is plural, so it means at least two.

phrases.english: "stacte, and onycha, and galbanum": that makes five,
and the other "spices": five more,
that makes ten,
"and pure frankincense": one,
that makes eleven.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק for רבי יוחנן's count of eleven.

steps.title: Maybe the פסוק is a כלל ופרט וכלל with no fixed number
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges רב הונא's reading: perhaps 'spices, three named spices, spices' is a כלל ופרט וכלל, which would include any item that burns and spreads a scent.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say: 'spices' is a general term, 'stacte, onycha, and galbanum' is a detail, and 'spices' is a general term again. With a כלל ופרט וכלל, you include only things like the detail. Just as the detail is something that burns, rises, and spreads its scent, so too anything that burns, rises, and spreads its scent.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks רב הונא's counting by suggesting a different way to read the same פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Using the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל, the word 'spices' would not mean a set number. It would include every item similar to the named spices: anything whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads. This would knock out the exact count of eleven.

keyTerms.meaning: General term, detail, general term: a rule for reading פסוקים

steps.whyThisMatters: If the challenge stands, the קטורת would have no fixed list of ingredients, which goes against רבי יוחנן's eleven.

phrases.english: But say: "spices" is a general term,
"stacte, and onycha, and galbanum" is a detail,
"spices": it went back and made a general term again.
A general term, a detail, and a general term:

phrases.aramaic: אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.
Just as the detail spells out
an item whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁקִּיטֵּר וְעוֹלֶה וְרֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף.
phrases.english: so too any item whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הונא's reading of the פסוק in step 12.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's counting of eleven ingredients from the פסוק
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same words can be read as a כלל ופרט וכלל, which includes all similar fragrant items instead of giving an exact number.

steps.title: Each named spice is needed, so the challenge stands
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא blocks a possible defense of רב הונא. Someone might argue that a כלל ופרט וכלל would only need one example. But נטף, שחלת and חלבנה are each needed for their own reason, so a כלל ופרט וכלל reading still works.
steps.simpleTranslation: You might say: if this is a general-detail-general pattern, the פסוק should have written just one detail! No, each detail is needed. If it wrote only נטף (a tree product), I'd think only tree spices count and not things grown from the ground, so it wrote שחלת. If it wrote only שחלת (grown from the ground), I'd think tree spices don't count, so it wrote נטף. And חלבנה had to be written for itself, because it smells bad and we would never include it otherwise.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא imagines a way to rescue רב הונא's count and then knocks it down. This keeps the challenge from Step 13 alive.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The suggested defense was: three examples are too many for a simple כלל ופרט וכלל, so the words must be counting ingredients. The גמרא answers that נטף and שחלת each teach a different kind of spice (tree and ground). חלבנה is needed because its bad smell would otherwise keep it out. So all three details fit a כלל ופרט וכלל, and רב הונא's count is still under attack.

keyTerms.meaning: a detail; a specific example in the פסוק
they are truly necessary; each one teaches something
a type of tree; a spice that comes from a tree
it comes for itself; it teaches only about its own inclusion

phrases.english: And if you would say: if so,
let the verse write just one detail!
Indeed, they are all necessary,
for if it had written "stacte," I would have said:
a type of tree, yes,
but things grown from the ground, no;
because of this it wrote "and onycha."
And if it had written "and onycha," I would have said:
things grown from the ground, yes,
but a type of tree, say no;
because of this it wrote "stacte."
And galbanum comes for itself,
because its smell is bad!

steps.triggerLanguage: וְכִי תֵימָא, אִם כֵּן, לִכְתּוֹב קְרָא חַד פְּרָטָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Strengthens the challenge of Step 13 by rejecting a possible defense of רב הונא.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The suggested defense that three named spices are too many for a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: Each named spice teaches something different (tree, ground, bad-smelling), so all three are needed even in a כלל ופרט וכלל.

steps.title: The general term already comes from 'take for yourself'
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers the challenge. If the פסוק needed a general term, 'קח לך' could serve as one. So the first 'סמים' is extra, and it must be counting ingredients, as רב הונא said.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, the general term could be learned from 'Take for yourself.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא finally answers the challenge against רב הונא. The first word 'סמים' cannot be needed as a general term, so it must be counting ingredients.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For a כלל ופרט וכלל you need a general word at the start. The words 'קח לך' already work as that general opening. That makes the word 'סמים' unnecessary for a כלל, so we use it as רב הונא did: to count two ingredients.

steps.title: Maybe the second 'spices' also means only two
steps.stepSummary: A new challenge to רב הונא's count. Why should the second 'סמים' double the five before it? Maybe it means just two ingredients, like the first 'סמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But say that the later 'spices' means two ingredients, just like the first 'spices'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא raises a new problem with how רב הונא got to eleven. It asks why the second 'סמים' should count as five instead of two.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רב הונא read the second 'סמים' as matching everything listed before it. That made ten, and frankincense made eleven. The challenge says: the same word should mean the same thing both times, so it adds just two. That would give a total of eight, not eleven.

keyTerms.meaning: the later ones; the second mention
the earlier ones; the first mention

like the first "spices"!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending one part of רב הונא's reading, the גמרא now attacks another part.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הונא's claim that the second 'סמים' doubles the five before it.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The same word should mean the same amount each time, so the second 'סמים' should add only two.

steps.title: The word's position shows it doubles everything before it
steps.stepSummary: If the second 'סמים' meant only two, the פסוק would have written both 'סמים' together and then the named spices. Since it was placed after the named spices, it matches all of them.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק write 'spices, spices' together, and at the end write 'stacte, and onycha, and galbanum.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge from Step 16 by pointing to where the second 'סמים' appears in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If both 'סמים' meant two each, there was no reason to split them up. The פסוק could have put them side by side. Placing the second one after the named spices shows it is counted against everything before it. That gives five plus five, as רב הונא said.

phrases.english: If so, let it write "spices" "spices" together,
and at the end let it write "stacte, and onycha, and galbanum."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16.

steps.terutzHavaAmina: The second 'סמים' adds only two, like the first.
steps.terutzMaskana: Its placement after the named spices shows it equals all five before it.
steps.whatToRemember: רב הונא's count of eleven holds up. The first 'סמים' is not needed as a general term because 'קח לך' does that job. The second 'סמים' doubles everything before it because of where it is placed.

steps.title: The school of רבי ישמעאל reads the פסוק as a general-detail-general pattern
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל reads 'סמים, נטף שחלת וחלבנה, סמים' as a כלל ופרט וכלל. This includes anything like the named examples: something whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads.
steps.simpleTranslation: The school of רבי ישמעאל taught: 'spices' is a general term; 'stacte, onycha and galbanum' is a detail; 'spices' is a general term again. With general-detail-general, you only include things like the detail. The detail is something whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads, so anything whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads is included.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא from the school of רבי ישמעאל that learns a כלל ופרט וכלל from the same words. This sets up the next discussion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא uses the rule of כלל ופרט וכלל. Under that rule, the general words include only items similar to the named examples. The shared quality of נטף, שחלת and חלבנה is that their smoke rises and their scent spreads. So any such item would qualify. This does not clash with the count of eleven. As רש״י explains, the school of רבי ישמעאל also needs eleven ingredients, and the ברייתא goes on to raise and answer the same question the גמרא just did.

keyTerms.meaning: similar to the detail; only things like the named examples

steps.confusionAlert: Don't read this ברייתא as arguing with רב הונא. רש״י says the school of רבי ישמעאל also counts eleven ingredients. The same words do two jobs: they give the count, and as a כלל ופרט וכלל they show what kind of spice qualifies.

phrases.english: The school of Rabbi Yishmael taught:
"Spices": a general term;
"stacte, onycha, and galbanum": a detail;
"spices": it went back and stated a general term.
A general term, a detail, and a general term:

phrases.english: you may include only things similar to the detail.
Just as the detail that is spelled out is
something whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads,

phrases.aramaic: אַף כׇּל דָּבָר שֶׁקִּיטֵּר וְעוֹלֶה וְרֵיחוֹ נוֹדֵף.
phrases.english: so too, anything whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After defending רב הונא, the גמרא brings a ברייתא that reads the same words as a כלל ופרט וכלל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is a כלל ופרט וכלל, including anything whose smoke rises and whose scent spreads.
steps.whyThisMatters: This ברייתא uses the very reading the גמרא pushed back against for רב הונא. That raises the question of how it fits with the count of eleven.

steps.title: The ברייתא raises and rejects another possible reading
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא asks whether the second כלל and פרט might mean something different. It rejects this and says we must stay with the first way of reading the פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: Or maybe the second general term is just like the first general term, and the detail is just like the first detail? You must say no. So you cannot learn by the later reading, only by the first reading.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא from step 18 continues. It suggests another way to read the פסוק and right away says that reading is wrong.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא already read the פסוק as a כלל ופרט וכלל. Now it asks: maybe the second 'סמים' and the details work differently? It rejects this, so the original כלל ופרט וכלל reading stays in place. What this question really means is explained in the next steps.

keyTerms.meaning: The second general term is treated just like the first general term
The detail is treated just like the first detail
The later suggested way of reading
The first way of reading (the כלל ופרט וכלל)

steps.confusionAlert: The ברייתא's words here are very short and unclear on their own. Don't try to fully understand them yet. The גמרא explains them in the next few steps.

phrases.aramaic: אוֹ אֵינוֹ אֶלָּא כְּלָל בִּכְלָל רִאשׁוֹן,
phrases.english: Or perhaps the general term is only like the first general term,
and the detail like the first detail?

phrases.english: So you cannot learn according to the later reading,

steps.title: What was the ברייתא's question?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the ברייתא's line again and asks what problem it was talking about.

steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא repeats the unclear line from the ברייתא and asks what it means. This sets up the explanation that comes next.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא raised a question without saying what it was really asking. The גמרא wants to know what reading the ברייתא had in mind before it rejected it.

phrases.english: Or perhaps the general term is only like the first general term,

steps.title: The second 'סמים' might mean only two
steps.stepSummary: The first half of the ברייתא's question was whether the second 'סמים' means only two spices, like the first. The answer is the same one the גמרא gave before: then the פסוק would have put both 'סמים' together.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what bothered him: the last 'spices' should mean two, just like the first 'spices' means two! Then he answered the way we answered: if so, the פסוק should have written 'spices, spices, נטף, שחלת and חלבנה.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the first part of the ברייתא's question. It is the same question and answer we already saw in steps 16 and 17.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'כלל בכלל ראשון' means: maybe the second 'סמים' works like the first and only adds two spices. The ברייתא rejects this the same way the גמרא did earlier. If that were true, both 'סמים' would sit together before the named spices. Since the second 'סמים' comes after them, it matches them.

phrases.english: And what does "the detail like the first detail" mean?

steps.title: Maybe לבונה זכה is also one of the examples
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא was asking about לבונה זכה. We already learn tree spices from נטף and ground-grown spices from שחלת. So maybe we should also learn from לבונה זכה and include anything whose scent spreads, even if its smoke does not rise.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what was bothering him: we learn kinds of trees from נטף, and things that grow from the ground from שחלת. So let us also learn from לבונה זכה, which adds one feature: we should include something whose smell spreads, even though its smoke does not rise up!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the second half of the ברייתא's question. Maybe לבונה זכה, which is named later in the same פסוק, should also count as an example.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each named spice teaches its own kind: נטף teaches tree spices and שחלת teaches ground-grown spices. So maybe לבונה זכה teaches a kind too: anything whose scent spreads, even if its smoke does not rise. That would make the rule wider than what step 18 said.

keyTerms.meaning: Things that grow from the ground

phrases.english: This is what was bothering him:
kinds of trees are learned from stacte,

that we should include something whose scent spreads

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָא קַשְׁיָא לֵיהּ מִינֵי אִילָנוֹת יָלְפִי מִן נָטָף

steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: 'פרט בפרט ראשון' means treating לבונה זכה as another example, which would include anything whose scent spreads even without rising smoke.

steps.title: לבונה זכה is outside the pattern, so it is not an example
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא rejects that reading. If לבונה זכה were meant as an example, the פסוק would have put it in the middle, between the two 'סמים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: He then said: if so, the פסוק should have written לבונה זכה in the middle, and you would learn from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא answers why לבונה זכה does not count as one of the examples. The answer comes from where it is placed in the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A כלל ופרט וכלל only uses the examples that sit between the two general terms. לבונה זכה comes after the second 'סמים', so it is outside that frame. So the rule stays as step 18 said: smoke that rises and a scent that spreads.

keyTerms.meaning: And you would learn from it

steps.whatToRemember: Both parts of the ברייתא's question are answered by looking at where the words sit in the פסוק. The second 'סמים' comes after the named spices, so it matches them. לבונה זכה comes after the second 'סמים', so it is not one of the examples.
steps.whyThisMatters: This keeps the rule from step 18 in place: to count, an ingredient must both send up rising smoke and spread its scent.

phrases.english: He then said: if so,
let the verse write pure frankincense in the middle,
phrases.notes: He means between the two 'סמים', together with נטף, שחלת and חלבנה.

phrases.english: and then you would learn from it.

steps.triggerLanguage: הֲדַר אָמַר אִם כֵּן נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא לִלְבוֹנָה זַכָּה בְּמִיצְעֵי

steps.title: Putting frankincense in the middle would make twelve ingredients
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the claim that the פסוק would have put לבונה זכה in the middle: that would make twelve ingredients instead of eleven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If the פסוק had written 'pure frankincense' in the middle, there would be twelve ingredients!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on the last step. Putting לבונה זכה in the middle would ruin the count of eleven spices.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The second 'סמים' doubles whatever comes before it. If לבונה זכה stood before it, it would be doubled too, giving twelve. So the פסוק may have had a good reason to put לבונה זכה at the end, and the proof from step 24 seems weak.

keyTerms.meaning: Pure frankincense, one of the incense ingredients

phrases.english: If it would write 'pure frankincense' in the middle,
phrases.notes: The middle means between the two times the פסוק says 'סמים'.

phrases.english: there would be twelve!
phrases.notes: The second 'סמים' doubles everything before it, so frankincense would be counted twice, making twelve instead of eleven.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִי כַּתְבַיהּ לְבוֹנָה זַכָּה בְּמִיצְעֵי, הָוַיִין תְּרֵי עָשָׂר

steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that the פסוק would have placed לבונה זכה in the middle if it were meant as an example

steps.title: The verse could have moved galbanum to the end
steps.stepSummary: The answer: the פסוק could have put לבונה זכה in the middle and moved חלבנה to the end, keeping the count at eleven.
steps.simpleTranslation: If so, let the פסוק write 'pure frankincense' in the middle and 'galbanum' at the end.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The פסוק could have swapped the order and kept eleven, so putting לבונה זכה at the end must mean it is not an example to learn from.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Swapping לבונה זכה and חלבנה would keep the total at eleven. Since the פסוק did not do this, the order is deliberate. That means לבונה זכה is not meant as a model for adding spices whose smoke does not rise.

phrases.english: If so, let the verse write
'pure frankincense' in the middle,
and 'galbanum' at the end.

steps.triggerLanguage: אִם כֵּן, נִכְתּוֹב קְרָא לְבוֹנָה זַכָּה בְּמִיצְעֵי, וְחֶלְבְּנָה לְבַסּוֹף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 25

steps.terutzMaskana: The פסוק could have swapped לבונה זכה and חלבנה, so its place at the end is deliberate and it is not an example to learn from.
steps.whatToRemember: The incense allows only ingredients whose smoke rises. לבונה זכה is placed at the end on purpose, so we do not learn from it to add spices that only give off scent.

steps.title: ריש לקיש learns it from the word 'קטורת' itself
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש gives a simpler source: the word קטרת means something that makes smoke and rises.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said: we learn it from the word itself. What does 'קטרת' mean? Something that makes smoke and rises.
steps.whatsHappening: ריש לקיש offers a different source for the rule that only rising-smoke spices belong in the incense. He learns it from the meaning of the word קטרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is no need for the long reading of the order of the פסוק. The name itself describes rising smoke, so anything whose smoke does not rise is not 'קטרת'.

keyTerms.meaning: Incense; from a root meaning smoke

phrases.english: Reish Lakish said: from the word itself,
what does the word 'ketoret' mean?
Something that makes smoke and rises.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The word קטרת itself means rising smoke, so only ingredients whose smoke rises qualify.

steps.title: A fast must include sinners, just as galbanum is in the incense
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון חסידא teaches that a fast without some sinners of Israel is not a real fast, because the bad-smelling חלבנה is counted among the incense spices.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנא בר ביזנא said in the name of רבי שמעון חסידא: any fast that does not include some of the sinners of Israel is not a fast, since galbanum smells bad and the פסוק counts it with the incense spices.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a side lesson connected to חלבנה. Just as a bad-smelling spice is part of the incense, sinners must be part of a communal fast.
steps.deeperAnalysis: חלבנה alone smells bad, yet it belongs in the holy incense. In the same way, a communal fast must include everyone, even those who sinned.

phrases.english: Rav Chana bar Bizna said
Rabbi Shimon Chasida said:
Any fast that does not have in it
some of the sinners of Israel
is not a fast,
for galbanum's smell is bad
and the verse counted it with the incense spices.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָא בַּר בִּזְנָא אָמַר רַבִּי שִׁמְעוֹן חֲסִידָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A side teaching sparked by the mention of חלבנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A communal fast must include sinners of Israel, as shown by חלבנה being part of the incense.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known teaching about including every Jew, even sinners, in communal prayer and fasting.

steps.title: אביי's source: the people as one bundle
steps.stepSummary: אביי brings a different source for the same idea: a פסוק that speaks of God's 'bundle' established on the earth.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: we learn it from here: 'And His bundle He established on the earth.'
steps.whatsHappening: אביי offers another source for including sinners in a fast. He brings a פסוק about a bundle.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A bundle holds many pieces together. When the people are tied together as one, including sinners, they stand firm on the earth.

keyTerms.meaning: A bundle; a group tied together
From here; introduces a different source

phrases.english: Abaye said: from here:
'And His bundle He established on the earth.'

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The idea of including sinners is learned from the image of God's bundle established on the earth.

steps.title: Back to the mishnah: one who smears the anointing oil
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא returns to the משנה's list and quotes its next case: one who smears the שמן המשחה.
steps.simpleTranslation: And one who smears with the anointing oil.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next topic. It quotes the משנה's case of smearing the holy anointing oil, which carries כרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This line only opens the new discussion. The next steps explain who counts as a person for this law.

keyTerms.meaning: One who smears or applies oil

phrases.english: And one who smears with the anointing oil.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns from the side teaching to the next case in the משנה
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The משנה lists smearing שמן המשחה among the sins carrying כרת.

steps.title: ברייתא: who is exempt for smearing the oil
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא teaches that smearing the oil on animals, vessels, gentiles or corpses is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: one who smears the anointing oil on an animal or vessels is exempt; on gentiles or dead bodies, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that limits the law. Only smearing on certain bodies brings liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא lists four cases with no liability. The גמרא will next ask for the reason behind each one.

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught:
One who smears the anointing oil
on an animal or vessels is exempt,
on gentiles or dead bodies is exempt.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנוּ רַבָּנַן: הַסָּךְ בְּשֶׁמֶן הַמִּשְׁחָה לִבְהֵמָה וְכֵלִים פָּטוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a ברייתא defining the limits of the משנה's case
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing שמן המשחה on animals, vessels, gentiles or corpses brings no liability.

steps.title: Animals, vessels and corpses are not a person, but why gentiles?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands why animals, vessels and corpses are exempt, but asks why gentiles are exempt, since they seem to be people.
steps.simpleTranslation: It makes sense for animals and vessels, since it says 'On the flesh of a person it shall not be smeared,' and they are not a person. Corpses too: once someone dies he is called a 'dead body,' not a 'person.' But gentiles, why exempt? They are people!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains three of the exemptions using the word אדם in the פסוק. Then it challenges the fourth, gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק forbids smearing on 'בשר אדם'. Animals, vessels and corpses are clearly not called אדם. Gentiles are human, so the ברייתא's exemption for them seems to contradict the פסוק.

phrases.english: It makes sense for animals and vessels,
as it is written: 'On the flesh of a person it shall not be smeared,'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:32

phrases.english: and animals and vessels are not a person.
Dead bodies are also exempt,
since once he has died,
he is called a 'dead body,' and not a 'person.'
But gentiles, why is he exempt?
They are people!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges one ruling of the ברייתא in step 31
steps.kashyaTarget: The ברייתא's exemption for smearing the oil on gentiles
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק forbids smearing on 'בשר אדם', and gentiles appear to be included in the word אדם.

steps.title: A פסוק in יחזקאל shows how the word אדם is used here
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא answers from a פסוק in יחזקאל that calls the Jewish people 'אדם', which it reads as limiting the word אדם for this law.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, since it is written: 'And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture, you are אדם.' You are called 'אדם', and the gentiles are not called 'אדם'.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge with a פסוק in יחזקאל. It reads that פסוק as defining who the word אדם refers to in this law.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק speaks to Israel and says 'you are אדם'. The גמרא learns from this that the word אדם in the פסוק about the oil means Israel, so smearing on gentiles brings no liability.
steps.confusionAlert: This step is about how the word אדם is read in the פסוק of the anointing oil for this specific law. Do not read it as saying gentiles are not human; the גמרא itself just said 'they are people'.

phrases.english: No,
as it is written: 'And you, My sheep, the sheep of My pasture,
you are adam'
phrases.notes: יחזקאל 34:31

phrases.english: you are called 'adam'
and the gentiles are not called 'adam'.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָאיֵי, דִּכְתִיב: וְאַתֵּן צֹאנִי צֹאן מַרְעִיתִי אָדָם אַתֶּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 32
steps.terutzResolutionType: Defines a word in the פסוק using another פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gentiles are included in 'בשר אדם', so smearing the oil on them should bring liability.
steps.terutzMaskana: Based on the פסוק in יחזקאל, the word אדם in this law refers to Israel, so smearing the oil on gentiles brings no liability.
steps.whatToRemember: Liability for smearing שמן המשחה depends on the word 'בשר אדם'. Animals, vessels and corpses are excluded by the plain meaning, and gentiles are excluded based on the פסוק in יחזקאל.

steps.title: Challenge: gentile captives are called אדם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects with a פסוק from the war with מדין, where gentile captives are called 'נפש אדם'.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And the people (נפש אדם) were sixteen thousand'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the answer from step 33. It shows a פסוק that uses the word אדם for gentiles.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 33 said only Jews are called אדם, so smearing a gentile is exempt. But the captives of מדין were gentiles, and the תורה still calls them אדם. So the limit from יחזקאל seems wrong.

keyTerms.meaning: But isn't it written? (an opening for a challenge from a פסוק)

phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And the people were sixteen thousand'!
phrases.notes: במדבר 31:40, about the captives from מדין, who were gentiles.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the source reading given in step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only Jews are called אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A פסוק calls gentile captives 'נפש אדם', so gentiles are also called אדם.

steps.title: There, אדם only separates people from animals
steps.stepSummary: In that פסוק, the word אדם is only used to tell the captured people apart from the captured animals.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That is to exclude animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The answer: in the מדין פסוק, 'אדם' is not a special title. It simply marks people as opposed to animals.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The same פסוקים list the animals taken as spoils too. So the word אדם there only says 'humans, not animals.' That is different from the special meaning of אדם for the law of the oil.

phrases.english: He said to him:
That is to exclude animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק calls gentiles אדם in the full sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: There, אדם only contrasts people with animals.

steps.title: Challenge: the people of נינוה are called אדם
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא objects again from יונה, where the gentiles of נינוה are called אדם.
steps.simpleTranslation: But it is written: 'And should I not have pity on נינוה' and so on!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a second פסוק where gentiles are called אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק goes on to speak of more than 120,000 אדם in נינוה, and they were gentiles. This is another case of gentiles being called אדם.

keyTerms.meaning: נינוה, the gentile city יונה was sent to

phrases.aramaic: וְהָכְתִיב: ״וַאֲנִי לֹא אָחוּס עַל נִינְוֵה וְגוֹ׳״!
phrases.english: But isn't it written: 'And should I not have pity on נינוה,' and so on!
phrases.notes: יונה 4:11. The rest of the פסוק speaks of 120,000 'אדם' there, and also many animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second challenge against step 33.
steps.kashyaTarget: The claim that only Jews are called אדם
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The gentiles of נינוה are called אדם.

steps.title: Same answer: there too it separates people from animals
steps.stepSummary: The word אדם in יונה also only separates people from the animals mentioned in the same פסוק.
steps.simpleTranslation: That is to exclude animals.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the same answer as before.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק itself ends with 'and also many animals.' So אדם there just means 'people, not animals,' not the special meaning used for the oil.

phrases.english: That is to exclude animals.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 36 the same way step 35 answered step 34.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The people of נינוה are called אדם in the full sense.
steps.terutzMaskana: The word only contrasts them with the animals in the פסוק.

steps.title: A second reason gentiles are exempt
steps.stepSummary: Another answer: only someone who is himself forbidden to smear the oil is a forbidden target. Gentiles are not forbidden, so smearing them is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: And if you want, say: as the תנא taught before רבי אלעזר: Whoever is included in 'smearing' is included in 'it shall not be smeared,' and whoever is not included in 'smearing' is not included in 'it shall not be smeared.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a different answer to the question of step 32, without relying on the word אדם.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule ties the two sides together: the person who is forbidden to smear the oil is the same kind of person it is forbidden to smear. Only Jews are commanded not to smear it. So a gentile cannot be a forbidden target either.

keyTerms.meaning: And if you want, say (introduces another answer)
He is included in / covered by
The prohibition 'it shall not be smeared'

phrases.english: And if you want, say instead:
As the תנא taught before רבי אלעזר:
Whoever is included in the law of smearing,
is included in 'it shall not be smeared,'
phrases.notes: From שמות 30:32. He means it is forbidden to smear the oil on him.

phrases.english: and whoever is not included in the law of smearing,
is not included in 'it shall not be smeared.'

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second, independent answer to the question of step 32.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Alternative reasoning (matching who smears with who is smeared)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Gentiles are people, so smearing them should be forbidden.
steps.terutzMaskana: Gentiles are not commanded about the oil, so they are not forbidden targets either.
steps.whatToRemember: Two reasons smearing a gentile is exempt: (1) only Jews are called אדם for this law; (2) only someone forbidden to smear can be a forbidden target.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: kings and כהנים are a מחלוקת
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא repeats the exemptions and adds a מחלוקת: smearing kings or כהנים makes one liable according to רבי מאיר, exempt according to רבי יהודה.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught in another ברייתא: One who smears the anointing oil on animals or vessels, on gentiles or corpses, is exempt. On kings or כהנים: רבי מאיר holds him liable, and רבי יהודה exempts him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a new ברייתא that adds the case of kings and כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part matches the ברייתא of step 31. The new part is about kings and כהנים who were already anointed with this oil. רבי מאיר holds that smearing them again makes one liable, and רבי יהודה exempts. The גמרא explains the reason for each side in steps 47–49.

phrases.english: It was taught in another ברייתא:
One who smears with the anointing oil
on an animal or vessels, on gentiles or corpses, is exempt;
on kings or on כהנים,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר מְחַיֵּיב, וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה פּוֹטֵר.
phrases.english: רבי מאיר holds him liable, and רבי יהודה exempts him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a parallel ברייתא that adds new cases.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Smearing animals, vessels, gentiles or corpses is exempt. For kings and כהנים, רבי מאיר says liable and רבי יהודה says exempt.

steps.title: How much oil makes one liable
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא continues: רבי מאיר says any amount, רבי יהודה says a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: And how much must he smear to be liable? רבי מאיר says: any amount. רבי יהודה says: a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא now asks about the minimum amount of oil for liability.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר is strict: even a tiny bit counts. רבי יהודה requires an olive's volume. This sets up the next question, since רבי יהודה just said 'exempt.'

phrases.english: And how much must he smear and be liable?
רבי מאיר says: any amount.
רבי יהודה says: an olive's volume.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the same ברייתא with a second מחלוקת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר: liable for any amount. רבי יהודה: only for a כזית.

steps.title: But רבי יהודה said exempt
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how רבי יהודה can give a minimum amount for liability when he just said 'exempt.'
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יהודה say: exempt!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא points out what looks like a contradiction inside רבי יהודה's view in the ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If רבי יהודה exempts, why does he say how much makes one liable? The two parts of the ברייתא seem to clash.

keyTerms.meaning: But didn't he say? (points to an earlier statement to show a contradiction)

steps.confusionAlert: רבי יהודה did not exempt all smearing. His 'exempt' was only about kings and כהנים, as the next step explains.

phrases.english: But didn't רבי יהודה say: exempt!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Sets the two parts of the ברייתא against each other.
steps.kashyaTarget: רבי יהודה's view that a כזית makes one liable
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: He already ruled 'exempt,' so a minimum for liability makes no sense.

steps.title: רבי יהודה exempts only for kings and כהנים
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה's 'exempt' was only about kings and כהנים. For an ordinary person he holds one liable, with a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: When רבי יהודה exempts, it is regarding kings and כהנים. Regarding an ordinary person, he holds him liable.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by limiting רבי יהודה's 'exempt' to one case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The two rulings speak about different people. Kings and כהנים are exempt for רבי יהודה. Smearing an ordinary Jew makes one liable, and the כזית minimum applies there.

keyTerms.meaning: An ordinary person (not a king or כהן)

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה: smearing kings or כהנים is exempt; smearing an ordinary person makes one liable for a כזית. רבי מאיר: liable in both cases, for any amount.

phrases.english: When רבי יהודה exempts,
it is regarding kings and כהנים;
regarding an ordinary person, he holds him liable.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised in step 41.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the ruling to a specific case
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יהודה exempts all smearing of people.
steps.terutzMaskana: He exempts only kings and כהנים; for an ordinary person he holds one liable for a כזית.

steps.title: What is the root of their disagreement?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what point רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה actually argue about regarding the amount of oil.
steps.simpleTranslation: What exactly do רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. It asks for the reasoning behind the מחלוקת about any amount versus a כזית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 42 established that רבי יהודה also holds a person liable for smearing an ordinary person, but only with a כזית. Now the גמרא wants to know why רבי מאיר says any amount while רבי יהודה requires a כזית.

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי
phrases.english: Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda, about what do they disagree?

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה במאי פליגי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the reason behind the שיעור disagreement clarified in step 42.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The scriptural basis for any amount versus a כזית.

steps.title: רבי מאיר compares placing to smearing
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף explains that רבי מאיר links the 'placing' in the כרת verse to the 'smearing' in the warning verse. Smearing has no minimum, so placing has none either.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: This is what they argue about. רבי מאיר holds that the Torah wrote 'It shall not be smeared on a person's flesh,' and also wrote 'whoever places some of it on a זר.' Just as smearing means any amount, placing also means any amount.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף answers by explaining רבי מאיר's source. He reads the two neighboring פסוקים together.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The warning פסוק uses the word סיכה, smearing, and gives no minimum amount. רבי מאיר says the כרת פסוק's word נתינה, placing, refers to that same act. So it also has no minimum.

keyTerms.meaning: An outsider, someone not meant to be anointed

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: They disagree about this:
Rabbi Meir holds:
It is written, 'Upon the flesh of a person it shall not be smeared,'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:32

phrases.english: and it is written, 'and whoever places some of it upon a stranger,'
phrases.notes: שמות 30:33. This is the פסוק that gives the punishment of כרת.

phrases.english: just as smearing is any amount,
so too placing is any amount.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 43 by giving רבי מאיר's source.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי מאיר learns נתינה from the nearby סיכה, which has no minimum amount.

steps.title: רבי יהודה compares it to giving elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה learns the 'placing on a זר' from the word 'giving' used elsewhere in the Torah, which is measured by a כזית.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: We learn the 'placing on a זר' from 'giving' in general. Just as giving in general is a כזית, so too placing on a זר is a כזית.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף continues and explains רבי יהודה's source. He uses the same word נתינה as it appears elsewhere in the Torah.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה does not compare נתינה to the nearby word סיכה. He compares it to the same word, נתינה, in other places, where the standard measure is a כזית. That is why he requires a כזית for כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: The size of an olive, a standard minimum measure

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
We learn the 'placing' upon a stranger
from 'giving' in general.
Just as giving in general is an olive-bulk,
so too placing upon a stranger is an olive-bulk.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יהודה סבר ילפינן נתינה דעל זר מנתינה דעלמא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite side of the explanation begun in step 44.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה learns נתינה from נתינה elsewhere, which is a כזית.
steps.whatToRemember: Both learn from a comparison of words. רבי מאיר compares 'placing' to the nearby 'smearing,' so any amount counts. רבי יהודה compares it to 'giving' elsewhere, so a כזית is needed.

steps.title: For the מצוה of anointing, any amount works
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף adds that for the מצוה of anointing kings and כהנים, everyone agrees that any amount of oil is enough.
steps.simpleTranslation: But smearing to anoint kings and כהנים is any amount, according to everyone.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף limits the מחלוקת. The argument about a כזית applies only to the forbidden act. The מצוה of anointing works with any amount, according to both sides.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה's כזית rule comes from the word נתינה in the כרת פסוק. The מצוה of anointing is a separate matter called סיכה, so even רבי יהודה agrees it has no minimum.

phrases.english: But smearing in order to anoint kings and priests,
according to everyone, is any amount.

steps.triggerLanguage: אבל סיכה למימשח מלכים וכהנים דברי הכל כל שהוא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Limits the מחלוקת of steps 44 and 45 to the forbidden act only.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The מצוה of anointing kings and כהנים is done with any amount, according to everyone.
steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two cases. The כזית argument is about the forbidden smearing on a זר. The מצוה of anointing a king or כהן has no minimum, according to everyone.

steps.title: Why do they argue about kings and כהנים?
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף asks why רבי מאיר says one is liable for smearing kings and כהנים while רבי יהודה exempts it.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רב יוסף said: What do רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה disagree about regarding kings and כהנים?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רב יוסף turns to the second מחלוקת from the ברייתא in step 39: smearing kings and כהנים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This question is about who counts as a זר, not about the amount. It concerns kings and כהנים who were already anointed, so the מצוה of anointing them is finished.

phrases.english: And Rav Yosef said:

phrases.aramaic: בְּמַאי פְּלִיגִי רַבִּי מֵאִיר וְרַבִּי יְהוּדָה
phrases.english: About what do Rabbi Meir and Rabbi Yehuda disagree
regarding kings and priests?

steps.triggerLanguage: ואמר רב יוסף במאי פליגי רבי מאיר ורבי יהודה גבי מלכים וכהנים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the amount argument to the kings and כהנים argument.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: The reason for the מחלוקת over liability for smearing kings and כהנים.

steps.title: רבי מאיר: right now they are זרים
steps.stepSummary: רבי מאיר holds that an already-anointed king or כהן is now a זר, so smearing him makes one liable.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי מאיר holds: It is written 'whoever places some of it on a זר,' and a king and a כהן are now זרים.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains רבי מאיר's side. Once they have been anointed, the king and the כהן have no further מצוה of anointing, so they count as זרים now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי מאיר looks only at the present moment. Right now there is no מצוה to smear this person, so he fits the פסוק's word זר.

phrases.english: Rabbi Meir holds:
It is written, 'and whoever places some of it upon a stranger,'
and a king and a priest are strangers now.

steps.triggerLanguage: רבי מאיר סבר ואשר יתן ממנו על זר כתיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 47 for רבי מאיר.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A זר is judged by his present status. An anointed king or כהן is a זר now.

steps.title: רבי יהודה: a זר must be one from start to finish
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה holds that only someone who was always a זר counts. Kings and כהנים were not זרים at first, so smearing them is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יהודה holds: We need someone who is a זר from his beginning to his end, and a king and a כהן were not זרים at the start.
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף explains רבי יהודה's side. A person who was once meant to be anointed does not count as a זר for this prohibition.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה defines a זר more narrowly than רבי מאיר does. Since the king and כהן had a מצוה to be anointed at the beginning, they never fully become זרים, and smearing them carries no כרת.

keyTerms.meaning: From his beginning to his end

phrases.english: And Rabbi Yehuda holds:
We require that there be a stranger
from his beginning until his end,

phrases.aramaic: וּמֶלֶךְ וְכֹהֵן מֵעִיקָּרָא לָאו זָרִים הָווּ.
phrases.english: and a king and a priest were not strangers originally.

steps.triggerLanguage: ורבי יהודה סבר בעינן עד דאיכא זר מתחלתו ועד סופו
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבי יהודה's side, the opposite of step 48.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A זר must be a זר from beginning to end. Kings and כהנים were not, so smearing them is exempt.
steps.whatToRemember: רבי מאיר judges a person's status by the present moment. רבי יהודה requires him to be a זר from beginning to end.

steps.title: They follow their own approaches elsewhere
steps.stepSummary: רב איקא בריה דרב אמי says that רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה are each consistent with views they hold elsewhere, and he begins to quote a source.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב איקא the son of רב אמי said: And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught:
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is setting up the next move. רב איקא is about to show another place where these two תנאים argue in the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The claim is that this מחלוקת is not a one-time argument. It reflects a consistent way each תנא thinks, and the proof comes in the source that follows.

keyTerms.meaning: They follow their own reasoning, staying consistent with their views elsewhere

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַב אִיקָא בְּרֵיהּ דְּרַב אַמֵּי:
phrases.english: Rav Ika, son of Rav Ami, said:
And they follow their own reasoning, as it was taught:

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רב איקא בריה דרב אמי ואזדו לטעמייהו דתניא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces support showing that the views on kings and כהנים in steps 48 and 49 match these תנאים' rulings elsewhere.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: רבי מאיר and רבי יהודה each follow a consistent approach that appears elsewhere.
